item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00295","decision":"none","candidate_ranking":["C22","C24","C16"],"selected_candidate_label":null,"confidence":0.93,"relationship_type":"none","rationale":"C22 is the closest because it supplies the historical fact expressly used by the child—that the last World War II state of war ended on April 28, 1952—and both proclamations contain limiting clauses beginning “Nothing in this proclamation shall be construed.” But this is a shared factual predicate plus conventional savings language, not evidence that C22 supplied the child’s distinctive amnesty-and-pardon machinery. C24 similarly concerns termination of a World War II state of war, while C16 grants statutory relief from legal disabilities and includes a limitation clause, but neither parallels the child’s constitutional pardon, specified class of deserters, or remission of citizenship and nationality consequences. No candidate supplies a concrete, material drafting template for those operative provisions.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the last of the states of war existing at that time was not formally and legally terminated until April 28, 1952","parent_excerpt":"the national emergencies declared to exist by the proclamations of September 8, 1939, and May 27, 1941, terminated this day upon the entry into force of the Treaty of Peace with Japan","explanation":"C22 supplies the same April 28, 1952 historical setting, but that setting is merely a factual premise in the child."},{"child_excerpt":"Nothing in this proclamation shall be construed as removing... any charge of desertion... or as pardoning, remitting, or mitigating any penalties... except as hereinbefore specifically provided.","parent_excerpt":"Nothing in this proclamation shall be construed to affect [the 1950 emergency]...; and nothing herein shall be construed to affect the continuation of the said emergency of September 8, 1939...","explanation":"C22 and the child both use a savings clause to confine the proclamation’s effects, but this is conventional legal drafting and the preserved matters are materially different."},{"child_excerpt":"fully remitted as to such persons any relinquishment, loss, or forfeiture of their rights... capacities, or nationality","parent_excerpt":"there has existed... such disruption or suspension of facilities... and... the time within which compliance with such conditions and formalities may take place is hereby extended","explanation":"C16 likewise grants targeted relief from statutory consequences and then limits its reach, but its copyright-extension mechanism does not materially match the child’s exercise of the pardon power."}]}
